articles.title: Novak Djokovic’s  US Open shocker: All the records broken during his first-round exit
articles.summary: Tennis News: Novak Djokovic’s first-round defeat at the 2026 US Open may have ended his campaign earlier than expected, but the match produced several significant .
articles.body: Novak Djokovic’s first-round defeat at the 2026 US Open may have ended his campaign earlier than expected, but the match produced several significant records and milestones for both the Serbian great and his opponent Mariano Navone.The match marked Djokovic’s 20th appearance at the US Open, making him only the fourth man in men’s singles to reach the landmark. He joined Jimmy Connors, Andre Agassi and Feliciano Lopez in the exclusive group.“I'm very proud of that,” Djokovic said. “Obviously, longevity was always one of the goals when I was younger: trying to have long career, trying to have more shots at Grand Slam and stay healthy long enough so that I can perform for as many years as possible.”Djokovic has appeared at every US Open since making his debut in 2005, except in 2017 when a right elbow injury forced him to miss the tournament. He has won the title four times, in 2011, 2015, 2018 and 2023.His first US Open match, a five-set marathon against Gael Monfils, came two decades ago. Monfils, who is planning to retire, is also competing at this year’s tournament.“Here we are 20 years later,” Djokovic said. “We're both still grinding and representing the older generation.”Records broken and made during this historic nightWhile Djokovic added another longevity record, his defeat to Navone brought one of his most remarkable Grand Slam streaks to an end. Navone stunned the 24-time major champion 7-6, 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 to record the biggest victory of his career.The defeat snapped Djokovic’s streak of 78 consecutive first-round wins at Grand Slam tournaments. It was his first opening-round loss at a major since the 2006 Australian Open, ending a run that had lasted nearly two decades.The four-hour, 36-minute battle also became the longest first-round match in a major tournament in Djokovic’s professional career.For Navone, the victory was the biggest of his career.For Djokovic, it was a night of contrasting milestones, his 20th US Open appearance ended with his earliest exit from the tournament and the loss of one of his longest-standing Grand Slam streaks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open: As Venus Williams falls in a match that ends at 2 a.m., the sport must examine its scheduling problem
articles.summary: Venus Williams' first-round match against Sofia Kenin didn't start until 12:15 a.m. in New York. That's a lot to ask of people who pay for tickets.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Nobody who bought a ticket to Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first night of the US Open expected to watch Venus Williams beat Sofia Kenin, and she did not.

Instead, the bare minimum expectation was that the match would actually be played on Sunday — you know, the day it was scheduled.

Taking the court after midnight on Monday and finishing later than any first-round match in US Open history, the 46-year old who won this event in 2000 and 2001 did what she has done every other time she's played in a singles tournament this year. She lost 6-2, 7-6 (8-6), dropping her record to 0-12 this year and 1-15 since last summer when she started asking for wild cards to get in events that her ranking (currently No. 618) would not otherwise allow her to play.

While trying not to be unkind here, it should be obvious to everyone — Williams most of all — that it's time for this comeback to end. Wild cards are meant to be given at the tournament's discretion, but even for someone who has meant and given as much to tennis as she has, there needs to be a limit. Williams is no longer competitive as a singles player, and putting her in a Grand Slam field at this stage feels decidedly unserious.

But it's not as unserious as starting a sporting event after midnight.

Let's back up for a moment before we get in the weeds on this one. Tennis, in general, has a scheduling problem at the Grand Slams.

It's bad enough that when you buy a ticket to one of these events, you don't know until the day before who you're going to see or what time they're going to play. That's a strain on fans, but it's kind of unavoidable.

On the other hand, there are ways to ensure that tournaments aren't cheating their ticket-buying customers. And whether it's Wimbledon's 11 p.m. curfew that forces matches to finish the next day or the matches in Australia, Paris and New York that last until the wee hours of the morning, tennis is simply asking too much of the people who pay their hard-earned money to come to these events.

Look, there have been some classic, memorable matches at the US Open that lasted until 3 a.m. But the bigwigs in this sport have become entirely too comfortable with how often it happens, largely shrugging their shoulders whenever it comes up.

The US Open night session includes two matches — one men's and one women's match. The beauty of tennis and the problem with tennis is that there's no clock. A women's match could be 45 minutes or 3 1/2 hours. A men's match, played in a best-of-five set format, could be 90 minutes or 5 hours.

And you can't predict what's going to happen. Nobody would have expected Novak Djokovic to play more than 4 1/2 hours before losing to Mariano Navone to begin Sunday's night session. That's why it took so long for Williams and Kenin to get on the court.

Logically, it would be better to put a women's match first so that there's no danger of waiting for a five-setter. But that's also a TV decision involving which players ESPN wants to have in the heart of their primetime window. And ESPN's vote matters — after all, they pay a lot of money for the rights to broadcast this event.

Nobody's come up with a great solution for this.

The Australian Open has a similar problem to the US Open and will occasionally have matches that spill well into the next day. The French Open started a standalone match for its night session a few years ago to sell as a separate TV package. They've been criticized because nearly all of those matches have been men's, with the reasoning being that you need to play a best-of-five in that slot rather than best-of-three to give ticket buyers the best chance at seeing a long enough match to justify the value. Wimbledon only has one session with three matches, and on a day where a couple of them go the distance, that causes problems because they are forced by local ordinance to shut down at 11 p.m.

In a perfect world, the US Open would start its night session earlier, but that idea has met resistance due to the difficulty of getting ticket buyers in the building on time if they're coming from New York after work.

So, again, there are real problems no matter how you do it.

But starting a match after midnight and finishing just after 2 a.m. isn't fair to fans, tournament officials or players. And it certainly wasn't a great look for the US Open to put one of its former champions out there at such a late hour, in front of a mostly empty stadium, for what should ostensibly be her last-ever Grand Slam singles match. What's the point of a goodbye if most of the country is already asleep?

Even if Williams-Kenin had gone first, that doesn't solve the problem of how much it taxes everyone to conclude an evening of tennis so late. But until the sport's bigwigs get in a room and decide that it's unacceptable for matches to start at midnight, it'll keep happening.

These aren't easy problems, but you can't solve them if you never even try.

articles.title: Venus Williams: "A la una o las dos de la madrugada, no es fácil encontrar tu ritmo"
articles.standfirst: En el encuentro de inicio más tardío en este 'Grand Slam', la estadounidense perdió su decimoquinto partido consecutivo en el circuito, esta vez ante Sofia Kenin
articles.summary: En el encuentro de inicio más tardío en este 'Grand Slam', la estadounidense perdió su decimoquinto partido consecutivo en el circuito, esta vez ante Sofia Kenin
articles.body: La tenista estadounidense Venus Williams lamentó las dificultades de disputar un partido de madrugada tras caer ante su compatriota Sofia Kenin en la primera ronda del Abierto de Estados Unidos en la madrugada de este lunes. "Creo que tuve muchos buenos momentos hoy, sin duda. A medida que avanzaba el partido, seguí empujándome para intentar encontrar mi mejor tenis y encontrar mi ritmo. No es fácil hacerlo en una primera ronda. No es fácil hacerlo a la una o las dos de la madrugada e intentar encontrar tu ritmo y jugar tu mejor tenis, pero hice todo lo posible", explicó Williams tras el encuentro. La estadounidense, de 46 años, afrontó su vigésima sexta participación en el cuadro principal del Abierto estadounidense, que comenzó a las 00.13 horas, el inicio de un encuentro más tardío en el US Open, y pese a caer por 6-2 y 7-6 (9-7) tuvo opciones de forzar el tercer set. Williams, que perdía 2-4 en la segunda manga, reaccionó para ponerse 5-4 y dispuso de tres puntos de set al resto. En el desempate llegó a situarse 6-2 y tuvo otras cuatro oportunidades para hacerse con el parcial, pero Kenin salvó todas y cerró el partido a la primera oportunidad. "Creo que ella jugó bien", señaló Williams. "Tuve algunas oportunidades con su saque. Ella tuvo un gran segundo servicio. Quizá tuve algún punto suelto, pero no creo que simplemente lo regalara. Creo que fue un poco desafortunado, y creo que es uno de los mejores partidos que ha jugado últimamente", añadió. La derrota deja a Williams con un balance de 0-12 esta temporada y supone su quinta eliminación consecutiva en la primera ronda del Abierto de Estados Unidos. Su último triunfo se remonta a julio de 2025, ante su compatriota Peyton Stearns. Kenin, número 110 de la clasificación mundial, se enfrentará en segunda ronda a la también estadounidense Jessica Pegula, tercera cabeza de serie.

articles.title: US Open: Mariano Navone wins battle as Novak Djokovic’s body says no
articles.summary: Tennis News: NEW YORK CITY: A champion’s challenge faded into the night as his body caved in on Arthur Ashe, while a younger pro kept his head and superbly pieced .
articles.body: NEW YORK CITY: A champion’s challenge faded into the night as his body caved in on Arthur Ashe, while a younger pro kept his head and superbly pieced his game together to find a way. There was heroism on both sides of the net on the US Open’s opening Sunday.For Mariano Navone, the 25-year-old ranked No. 49 in the world, it was more than staring down a legend who had a 37-0 career record in first and second rounds of the US Open. The compactly built Argentine produced a stirring level of tennis, backed by a firm resolve.For Novak Djokovic, the 24-time major winner, it was a stubborn refusal to give in amid extraordinary scenes on court. Through four hours and 40 minutes of physical torment, the 39-year-old, so unwell that he vomited more than once and required medical attention, even took a two set to one lead. Egged on by a crowd that stoked his spirit, Djokovic kept going, even when his body appeared to have nothing more to give.Navone, a clay-courter, adapted well on Sunday, particularly on the backhand side, to clinch his first five-set win in five matches, 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1.Djokovic, in the hunt for a 25th major title, said he felt awful on court and “pretty much despised every moment he spent on court” for that reason.“It's something that I've been carrying into pretty much every match this year. Vomiting, it’s a serious issue there. Then my whole body starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain. The back just gave up, in the end it was the shoulder, and I couldn't close it out,” Djokovic said. “I was a break up in the fourth, but struggled all the way since the fourth game of the match.”He added, “I don't want to take too much out of his win. Congrats to him. He's a fighter.”Djokovic didn’t elaborate on his health issue, but said he was trying to find a solution.The Serbian superstar said giving up did cross his mind. “But then I won a set and then a third one. Then I was, like, okay, maybe there is a chance,” he said. “I didn't want to give up in fourth or fifth, I wanted to finish the match.”The truth is that there’s no easy draw for Djokovic anymore.Not because of the quality of his opponents, but because of the expectations he carries onto court every time. Against an Alcaraz or Sinner, age offers an explanation when he loses. Against the likes of Navone, that doesn't count. At 39, Djokovic is expected to win, and win comfortably. But time is not moving to anyone’s bidding, and the other players in the draw know that.Navone, just 12-29 in tour-level matches on hard courts, had to raise his level mentally and physically in the first round. As ragged as Djokovic’s condition was, Navone still had to cross the line against a player of this stature, and that is never easy.“I never played on the Arthur Ashe, I never played against Novak before. It's the first time I won a five-set match. This moment we will remember for a long time,” Navone said. “For me, the mental part was the best one. I was two sets to one down, and then a break down also in the fourth, but in that moment I feel it. My game was better from there.”Even when Djokovic was throwing up behind the towel box, Navone put his head down and went about his business.“I understood he wasn't feeling very good,” he said. “It’s tough to play against him like this, because you have chances to win against him. I had to keep my mind in the moment, in my game, and the important things on my side. That’s the best thing I did.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Who is Pat Cash’s girlfriend Charlotte Hodson? All about the Former Wimbledon champion’s fiancee who is a singer and massage therapist
articles.summary: International Sports News: Former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash has announced his engagement to his girlfriend Charlotte Hodson. The Australian tennis legend, 61, shared the happy.
articles.body: Former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash has announced his engagement to his girlfriend Charlotte Hodson. The Australian tennis legend, 61, shared the happy news on social media after their relationship became public at Wimbledon last year. Cash won the Wimbledon men’s singles title in 1987 after beating Ivan Lendl in the final. He is now preparing for another major chapter in his life.Cash revealed the engagement on Instagram on Sunday. He shared a picture with Hodson and described her as his “soulmate”. The couple received congratulatory messages from friends, family and fellow tennis stars. Three-time Wimbledon champion Boris Becker was among those who celebrated the news.Who is Pat Cash’s girlfriend Charlotte Hodson?Charlotte Hodson is a singer, songwriter and massage therapist. She has built a career in both music and wellness. She is also familiar with the world of professional sport through her work as a massage therapist.Hodson is the vocalist for her band Chocolate Charlie. The group has performed as part of Cash’s show, The Pat Cash Experience. Her musical career has also seen her perform alongside some well-known names.According to her band’s website, Hodson has performed with British pop group Westlife, Danii Minogue and Saint Etienne. Her experience in music has therefore taken her beyond local performances and into larger entertainment circles.Hodson also works as a massage therapist through her brand, 8 Elements Massage. She is based in High Wycombe and has worked with Cash since as far back as 2023.Her work has also brought her into contact with professional athletes. She has provided massage therapy for tennis players Kayla Day and Li Tu. She has also worked with the Enduro Motorsports GT racing team.Hodson and Cash went public with their relationship during the Wimbledon tournament last year. Cash was working as a broadcaster at the event. Their appearance together attracted attention because of Cash’s long connection with the famous Grand Slam tournament.Cash eventually confirmed that their relationship had reached another important stage.The former Wimbledon champion announced their engagement to his Instagram followers. He posted a photograph of himself with Hodson and shared an emotional message about finding love.The announcement quickly attracted congratulatory messages. Becker was among those to send his best wishes to the couple. The three-time Wimbledon champion wrote: “Congratulations to both of you.”Hodson will now become part of Cash’s family. The Australian tennis star has four children. His first child was born when Cash was only 21.Cash remains closely connected to tennis despite retiring from professional competition. He has worked as a broadcaster and continues to be a familiar face around major tennis events.His relationship with Hodson has also developed alongside their professional interests. She has performed at events connected to Cash, while her massage therapy work has brought her into the sporting world.The couple’s engagement marks a new beginning for the former Wimbledon champion and the singer and therapist.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Novak Djokovic injuries: How every painful setback tested the tennis star, yet he rose each time to fight his way back
articles.summary: International Sports News: •;Novak Djokovic’s career has had almost everything a tennis player can face physically, from breathing problems and heat illness to serious elbow, sh.
articles.body: •;Novak Djokovic’s career has had almost everything a tennis player can face physically, from breathing problems and heat illness to serious elbow, shoulder, abdominal, hamstring and knee injuries. Some forced him to stop matches, while others came during Grand Slam runs. Yet Djokovic kept finding ways back. Even in 2026, after another difficult physical battle at the US Open, he is still competing at the highest level.Novak Djokovic’s major injuries and how he fought through them•2005 French Open: Djokovic retired against Guillermo Coria with a lower-back injury.•2006 French Open: He stopped against Rafael Nadal because of a back and thigh problem.•2007 Wimbledon: A badly infected blister on his left toe, along with back and overall physical problems, forced him to retire against Nadal in the semifinals. Djokovic later said he did not want to make the injury worse.•2009 Australian Open: Djokovic retired against Andy Roddick after struggling with heat illness, cramps and soreness in extreme conditions.•2010–11 health struggles: Djokovic had repeated breathing and energy problems during matches. He later changed his diet after identifying a sensitivity to gluten, which he credited with helping him feel stronger and more comfortable on court.•2016–18 right elbow injury: The elbow problem became a major setback and ended his 2017 season after Wimbledon. He had surgery in January 2018. Months later, he won Wimbledon and the US Open and finished the year as world No. 1.•2019 US Open: A left shoulder injury forced Djokovic to retire against Stan Wawrinka while trailing 6-4, 7-5, 2-1.•2021 Australian Open: Djokovic suffered an abdominal muscle tear during his match with Taylor Fritz but continued the tournament and won the title.•2023 Australian Open: He arrived with a left hamstring injury and needed heavy strapping and medical treatment during early rounds. He still defeated Stefanos Tsitsipas in the final to win his 10th Australian Open title.•2024 French Open: Djokovic tore the meniscus in his right knee during his fourth-round win over Francisco Cerúndolo. He withdrew from the tournament and had surgery. Just over eight weeks later, he won Olympic gold in Paris after beating Carlos Alcaraz.•2025: A continuing shoulder injury eventually forced Djokovic to withdraw from the ATP Finals after he had won the Athens title.•2026 US Open: Djokovic faced another physical test against Mariano Navone. He dealt with vomiting, cramps, back and shoulder pain during a four-hour, 36-minute first-round match before losing in five sets.Novak Djokovic’s recent injuries show the same fightThe 2026 US Open loss was very different from some of Djokovic’s famous injury comebacks because this time he could not find a way through. Still, the match showed why his physical struggles have become such an important part of his story. He had already dealt with health problems during the season, yet continued to compete.That attitude was clear after his 2024 knee surgery too. Djokovic did not simply return to tennis; he pushed himself back into Grand Slam and Olympic competition. He reached the Wimbledon final and then won Olympic gold only weeks after the operation.His career has therefore been shaped not only by the injuries themselves, but by what he did after each one. Some setbacks forced him away from the court, some tested him during matches, and some required surgery. Each time, Djokovic found another reason to continue.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Morgan Riddle reveals five Naomi Osaka lessons after Taylor Fritz split as tennis influencer returns ahead of US Open
articles.summary: International Sports News: Morgan Riddle has returned to the tennis spotlight with a new collaboration featuring Naomi Osaka, just months after her breakup with Taylor Fritz. Th.
articles.body: Morgan Riddle has returned to the tennis spotlight with a new collaboration featuring Naomi Osaka, just months after her breakup with Taylor Fritz. The tennis influencer shared five lessons she picked up from Osaka in an Instagram post on August 30. The partnership with wellness brand Olly also brought Riddle back into the sport she has been closely linked with for years, this time through her own work rather than her relationship with Fritz.Morgan Riddle shares Naomi Osaka lessons in new tennis collaborationRiddle shared a carousel on Instagram as part of her paid partnership with Olly, where Osaka is a global brand ambassador. Along with photos from their collaboration, she listed five things she said she learned from the four-time Grand Slam champion.Riddle wrote, “Things I learned from Naomi Osaka: match fits matter, protecting your peace is a competitive advantage, serving is harder than it looks, wellness is cool (and) ‘Rally for Yourself’.”The final message refers to Olly’s wider wellness campaign, which focuses on self-care and mental health. For Riddle, though, the post was also a chance to show a different side of her connection with tennis.Her name became widely known in the tennis world during her relationship with Fritz. The pair dated for almost six years before splitting earlier in 2026. After the breakup, Riddle said she did not plan to date another professional athlete.Still, she has made it clear that tennis remains part of her work and interests. Her latest collaboration with Osaka gives her another way to stay connected to the sport while building her own identity around it.Naomi Osaka and Taylor Fritz begin 2026 US Open campaignsThe timing of Riddle’s collaboration is especially fitting, with both Osaka and Fritz preparing to begin their 2026 US Open campaigns.Fritz is the No. 9 seed in the men’s singles draw and is set to face fellow American Darwin Blanch in the first round. The U.S. Open’s official website confirmed that Blanch earned his wild card after winning the USTA Boys’ 18s National Championships.Fritz will also be looking to improve on his 2024 run in New York, when he reached his first Grand Slam final before losing to Jannik Sinner. He remains one of the leading American hopes at the tournament.His latest match came at the Cincinnati Open, where Brandon Nakashima beat him 7-6(9), 4-6, 6-3 in the quarterfinals. The ATP Tour confirmed the result on August 21.Osaka, meanwhile, is the No. 13 seed and will face Anastasia Zakharova in the first round. The match is scheduled for Arthur Ashe Stadium, with Osaka entering as the higher-ranked player.The Japanese star last played in Toronto, where she reached the quarterfinals before losing to Elena Rybakina.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: La bielorrusa, vigente campeona, supera a la colombiana en dos sets
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka, ataviada con su inseparable colgante, empezó con éxito este lunes la defensa de la corona del US Open. La bielorrusa, que no depende de ella para salir de Nueva York con el número 1, sólo le vale ganar retener el título y esperar, dio buena cuenta de la colombiana Camita Osorio, por 6-2 y 6-4. Sabalenka vence pero no convence. No hay un partido cómodo para ella. Después de anotarse la manga inicial por la vía rápida, sufrió en la continuación. Osorio, la 59 de la WTA, la tuteó y aprovechaba los errores no forzados que procedían desde el otro lado de la red. No fue hasta el noveno juego del segundo set cuando se anotó la rotura definitiva.

articles.title: Safiullin - Alcaraz: resultado, resumen y estadísticas de la primera ronda del US Open
articles.summary: Lo dejamos por aquí hoy. Disponible la crónica del partido en MARCA. Seguro que seguiremos teniendo grandes noticias de Carlos Alcaraz en su camino en
articles.body:
Última hora del Safiullin - Alcaraz en directo:

Buenas tardes, bienvenidos a la segunda jornada del US Open 2026 y, por fin se puede decir, HOY JUEGA CARLOS ALCARAZ. Después de más de cuatro meses de espera, concretamente desde el 14 de abril cuando daba inicio la pesadilla del murciano con la lesión en la muñeca derecha que le obligó a retirarse en la segunda ronda del Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell, regresa a una pista de tenis. Y no podía ser en otro lugar que en Flushing Meadows, y teniendo como primera prueba un reto mayúsculo tras tantos meses de baja, un partido al mejor de cinco mangas. La pista Arthur Ashe, de 23.771 espectadores de capacidad, se prepara para recibir a los protagonistas de hoy: el fenómeno de El Palmar, campeón de siete 'majors', 26 títulos ATP y el más joven en completar el 'Career Grand Slam' (ganar los cuatro grandes) en la historia. Se enfrentará al ruso Roman Safiullin, alguien que ya sabe lo que significa ganar al español en una gran cita como es el Masters 1000 de París. El encuentro se disputará en el segundo turno de la ya nombrada Arthur Ashe, sobre la 13:30 h en Nueva York. En el primer partido del día, la número uno del mundo, Aryna Sabalenka, ha certificado su pase a la siguiente ronda ante la colombiana Camila Osorio por 6-2 y 6-4.

El encuentro tendrá un factor temporal muy importante. En el momento que salten ambos tenistas a pista, habrá un 70% de humedad con una temperatura de 24º. Para visualizar un partido de Alcaraz con estas condiciones o similares, hay que remontarse a febrero cuando se coronó como campeón de su primer Australian Open frente a Novak Djokovic, y ante la atenta mirada de su ídolo Rafa Nadal. Después de esto, el pupilo de Samu López se perdió los torneos de Madrid, Roma, Roland Garros, Wimbledon, Toronto y, el más reciente, Cincinnati.

El cara a cara entre ambos marca una victoria para cada uno. La primera, bajo techo, en el Masters 1000 de París 2023, donde se impuso el ruso por 6-3 y 6-4. La venganza de Carlos llegaría sobre la tierra de la Philippe Chatrier en los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024, con una cómoda victoria en sets corridos (6-4 y 6-2). Alcaraz luchará por volver al circuito de la mejor manera posible e intentar recuperar el nivel que le hizo coronarse en Australia y Doha a principios de año. Safiullin, por dar la campanada ante el defensor del título en La Gran Manzana de Nueva York.

articles.title: La primera decisión del US Open tras el fichaje de Craig Tiley: bajar los banquillos a la pista
articles.standfirst: Los técnicos podrán dialogar tranquilamente con los jugadores al estar más cerca
articles.summary: Los técnicos podrán dialogar tranquilamente con los jugadores al estar más cerca
articles.body: El pasado mes de febrero se confirmó el fichaje de Craig Tiley cuando nueva cabeza visible de la USTA en el Abierto de los Estados Unidos. El dirigente que había hecho grande al Open de Australia cambiaba de ciudad, Melbourne por Nueva York, y de continente. Con él a la cabeza del cuarto grande desde el pasado mes de julio, su primer cambio ha sido acercar el banquillo de los tenistas. La decisión que tomó para Australia en 2025 ya es una realidad en la presente edición del US Open. El equipo de los tenistas, en los estadios principales, se ha trasladado de la grada a una de las esquinas de la pista. Y la ausencia de micrófonos asegura la privacidad de las conversaciones. De esta forma se gana una mejor comunicación entre los entrenadores y sus pupilos. La imagen de los campeones saltando a la grada para abrazar a sus allegados se ha acabado. En el estreno de Carlos Alcaraz, su banquillo estaba formado por Samuel López (entrenador), Álvaro Alcaraz (entrenador y hermano), Juanjo Moreno (fisioterapeuta) y Albert Molina (agente).

articles.title: Bucsa y Selekhmeteva, primeras victorias de la 'Armada' femenina
articles.standfirst: La tenista cántabra superó a la checa Bejlek y Oksana ha acabado con la resistencia de la japonesa Ito
articles.summary: La tenista cántabra superó a la checa Bejlek y Oksana ha acabado con la resistencia de la japonesa Ito
articles.body: Cristina Bucsa ha recuperado su mejor tenis en el US Open, el grande donde el año pasado alcanzó los octavos. La tenista cántabra, la 40 del ranking, se ha cargado este lunes a una de las cabezas de serie. Sara Bejlek, vigésimo octava cabeza de serie, ha hincado la rodilla, por 7-4, 4-6 y 6-1, en 2 horas y siete minutos. Bejlek, que estrenó su palmarés de títulos este curso en Abu Dabi, llegaba con la vitola de semifinalista del WTA 1000 de Cincinnati. Sin embargo, Bucsa tiró de experiencia y maniató el juego de su rival. En la siguiente ronda espera la japonesa Himeno Sakatsume, la 144 de las listas. Cabe recordar que Cristina aterrizó en Nueva York con el casillero en blanco en cuanto a victorias en los Grand Slam en este 2026. Por su parte, Oksana Selekhmeteva, rusa de nacimiento pero española de pasaporte desde el último Roland Garros, se impuso ante Aoi Ito, por 6-2 y 6-4.

articles.title: US Open: Britain's Toby Samuel's meteoric rise from world No 1,871 and playing in Guatemala to the US Open second round
articles.summary: Britain's Toby Samuel is into the second round at Flushing Meadows where he takes on Czech 18th seed Jiri Lehecka; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Samuel, who came through qualifying to make his main draw debut at Flushing Meadows, needed just an hour and 32 minutes to beat the former world No 20 Tomas Machac and book his place in the second round.

The 23-year-old - dubbed the 'Winchester Rifle' due to his powerful serve - hammered down serves of up to 135mph to blow his Czech opponent away.

In doing so Samuel moved into the world's top 100 while earning £140,000, comfortably the biggest pay day of his career.

The win is the latest milestone in a remarkable rise for Samuel, who was ranked world No 1,871 in January 2025.

Since then, the former University of South Carolina alumnus has captured five ATP Challenger titles and reached his first ATP Tour semi-final at the Lexus Eastbourne Open in June.

"Yeah, it's kind of surreal," he said. "When I was obviously that ranking, I didn't even imagine I'd be playing these events this year.

"I was sort of hoping to be playing Challenger tournaments, and then obviously here now I've managed to carry on that form for the last year and haven't really looked back, so I'm just so happy I'm able to be in this situation now.

"I always had a good amount of belief because I was top at college for the last few years. I got to 400 and then I was injured, so that's obviously one of the reasons why my ranking was that low.

"I knew that I had the level to jump up and play here, but obviously not this fast.

"I've always believed in myself and obviously now it's paid off. I'm here now."

Life on the lowest rung of the tennis tour takes players to some weird and not-so-wonderful places, and Samuel recalled where he picked up his very first ranking point at a tournament in Guatemala in 2021 against Chilean player Michel Vernier and he won 13-11 in the third set to pocket $258 in prize money.

"It was 10pm at night, I was exhausted, I had five match points and I was just like to my mum, 'I want to fly home, I've got one point'.

"You have to go through all the tough experiences to be able to play at this level in the end, and those sort of build who you are as a character."

Samuel, who possesses a powerful serve and huge groundstrokes, says he is trying to hone his game so he can mix it with the very best.

"I have natural power, which is really helpful with tennis players, but having that power, you've got to be able to control it, because if you're missing a lot, it's not as effective as it can be.

"Definitely the last year, I've focused on being a tough competitor first, and then use those sort of weapons on top of that.

"I've been trying to learn how to use some more skills on the court. The last few months especially, I've been working my slice and my qualities in hand, which is the next step in my game, I think, to get to the next level."

He goes on to face 18th seed Jiri Lehecka in the next round, who beat Spain's Pablo Carreno Busta in four sets.

Samuel added: "He's one of the top guys in the game right now. He's such a good player and he's a big weapon, so I have to really try and stop him from playing his game when I play him the next match. It would be a good test to see where I'm at against those top guys again."

Speaking to Sky Sports , Tim Henman has been impressed with Samuel's meteoric rise.

"When you reflect on the way that's he's played in qualifying and then coming into a first round at a Grand Slam, against Tomas Machac, who is a quality player and to only lose seven games is a great achievement. This is another massive set for him. It's a huge opportunity, big points, enormous prize money that he can reinvest in his tennis and his team so why stop now? Hopefully he can keep going," said the former British No 1.

"He's really worked his way up in the rankings and with the Grand Slams there's that chance to win big. He really is moving in the right direction."

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.
authors: Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Harriet Dart beats Peyton Stearns to end 19-month wait for Grand Slam win
articles.summary: British qualifier Harriet Dart ends a 19-month wait for a Grand Slam singles win by fighting back to beat Peyton Stearns in the US Open first round.
articles.body:
Britain's Harriet Dart hailed the "community" of supporters who roared her on as she ended a 19-month wait for a Grand Slam win with a battling victory over Peyton Stearns at the US Open.

Cheered on by her parents, uncle, and numerous cousins at her "home away from home", Dart came back from a set and a break down to reach the second round in New York.

The 30-year-old had not won a main-draw singles match at a major since reaching the second round of the 2025 Australian Open.

She failed to qualify for four of the next six Grand Slams and fell at the first hurdle at the past two editions of Wimbledon after receiving a wildcard on each occasion.

Taken to three sets in all three of her US Open qualifying matches - including losing the opening set against Kristina Penickova and Heather Watson - Dart once again took the scenic route at Flushing Meadows.

She took advantage of the fluctuating form of American opponent Stearns, who is ranked more than 75 places above her, to win 3-6 6-3 6-2.

Dart, who will face 25th seed Marie Bouzkova in the second round, immediately ran to celebrate with her team, which now includes 2013 Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli.

The pair linked up in January and this latest win builds on a run to the quarter-finals at July's Challenger tournament in Vancouver and qualification for the Cincinnati Open in August.

"From her experience, she knows what I'm going through, how I'm feeling, how the day starts, how it finishes - everything from the little things to the big things," world number 131 Dart said of Bartoli.

"To be able to soak up everything, all of her experience, and learn from her - I feel I'm learning so much every time we speak.

"I feel like I'm improving at a lot of things, which motivates me."

Sabalenka wins to begin bid for US Open 'three-peat'

Venus Williams loses 15th match in row in 2am finish

Dart also said she had several family supporters dotted around New York.

"My uncle and cousins live here, one of my cousins from the UK is over at the moment, my mum has been here since I started in qualifying, and my dad flew in last night," she said.

"New York always feels like a home away from home.

"It feels like a community for me and I really felt the support out there."

Dart could not convert any of her four break points in the opening game of the match, with Stearns not offering up another opportunity in the first set.

Stearns piled relentless pressure on the Briton's serve, eventually breaking in the eighth game.

Dart was broken for a second time in the opening game of the second set but, aided by an increasingly erratic Stearns, whose 40 winners were offset by 47 unforced errors, she secured two breaks of her own to force a decider.

Seizing control midway through the third set, Dart completed a crucial hold in the sixth game to end a run of three consecutive breaks before converting her fourth match point to seal a nervy win in a little under two and a half hours.

Dart joins compatriots Toby Samuel and Katie Boulter in the second round.

images.caption: Image caption, Harriet Dart is through to the second round of the US Open for the third time, having previously reached that stage in 2022 and 2024

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Aryna Sabalenka beats Camila Osorio to begin 'three-peat' bid
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka blocks out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka blocked out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".

The two-time defending champion has suffered a dip in form in recent months after a stellar start to the season in which she reached the Australian Open final and completed the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami.

Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under serious threat and she risks ending the year without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022.

However, she avoided an early slip-up as she held off a resilient Osorio to win 6-2 6-4 on her return to Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I really feel my best emotions at this stadium so it means a lot to be back and have an opportunity for a 'three-peat'," Sabalenka said.

"I'm trying to focus on myself. I'm enjoying my time in New York and I'm ready to go out here and do anything it takes to get the wins.

When Sabalenka lifted the Miami Open trophy in April, she established a 3,000-point lead at the top of the world rankings.

But early exits - by her high standards at least - followed at the French Open and Wimbledon. Now, Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina, who faces American wildcard Thea Frodin on Tuesday, trails her by just 434 points.

It means that Sabalenka, who is defending 2,000 points at Flushing Meadows, will have to win the title and hope Rybakina falls before the semi-finals to extend her 99-week reign as world number one.

Home favourites Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff could also secure the number one ranking with a title triumph.

Should Sabalenka win a third successive US Open title, she would become only the third woman to do so in the Open era after Serena Williams and Chris Evert.

However, she will need to improve considerably to navigate a stacked draw in New York.

Sabalenka stormed through the first set against the 52nd-ranked Osorio but struggled in the second, landing 48% of her first serves and hitting 12 unforced errors.

But the four-time major singles champion fended off three break points and struck decisively at 4-4 before serving out victory after one hour and 28 minutes.

Sabalenka will face Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko next.

images.caption: Image caption, Aryna Sabalenka could become the first woman to win three successive US Open singles titles since Serena Williams in 2014

articles.title: US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York?
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic will turn 40 next May and after his shock exit in New York there is talk that the former world No 1 should call time on his career; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina .

Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.

The 39-year-old also admitted the underlying health issue he first revealed two weeks ago was "serious", although he remains intent on getting the problem fixed.

Djokovic looked physically spent, was repeatedly sick and regularly doubled over in pain. He held back tears at one point but managed a gracious smile as he congratulated world No 49 Navone on the biggest win of his career.

He has previously revealed that he plans to retire at the LA Olympics in 2028, draped in the flag of Serbia for one last time.

Former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli said: "It was so sad to watch. To see him suffer that much was heart-breaking.

"The way he was physically suffering is worrying. His health should come first, so he needs to have proper medical checks to see what happens."

Former British No 1 Tim Henman admitted defeat for Djokovic "was a tough watch" but does not think he should retire.

"Djokovic wasn't feeling well out on court. He gave it his absolute all to find a way through the match. When he was up two sets to one with a break in the fourth, you thought he could," said the former US Open semi-finalist.

"But he was vomiting on the court and didn't have the energy. Navone kept on fighting and, with youth on his side, he ran away with the fourth and fifth set."

On the idea of retirement, Henman said: "Absolutely not. It's his decision, it's his prerogative. He's No 5 in the world. If every person who was fifth best in the world at their occupation retired, there wouldn't be many people working. It's purely his decision. He should play for as long as he likes and I definitely don't think he should be stopping right now."

Asked whether an ailing Djokovic has what it takes physically anymore, Henman replied: "His mentality and will to win is still good enough [to win titles] but when you see the physical challenges of being 39 and what his body is going through and trying to find solutions - it's tough.

"When you hear him saying he 'despised being out there', that's awful.

"I'm sure he will go away and assess things because that's not the way we want to see Djokovic depart any tournament."

Ryan Harrison admits it's tough for Djokovic, who has been battling with his body after a nightmare stretch which also saw him lose in the first round of the Cincinnati Open earlier this month.

"It's frustrating whenever you're battling your body a little bit, but not enjoying the moment that you're in specifically because it's difficult is quite different from not enjoying the entirety of the sport," said Harrison.

"He'll want to get back in action in 2027. I still think he's a great player and he's still at the top of the game."

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Ben Shelton begins US Open run with Grand Slam drought in focus
articles.summary: Former Florida star Ben Shelton opens the US Open against Tallon Griekspoor with a chance to make a deep run.
articles.body:
Ben Shelton begins his US Open run on Monday night against Tallon Griekspoor in the first round at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

The former Gator has established himself as one of the top American men in the sport, sitting inside the top 10 all year. Taylor Fritz is the other top American, with Frances Tiafoe, Learner Tien and Brandon Nakashima also among the country's top players. All five are participating in the US Open, and they are looking to break one of the sport's most notable droughts.

No American man has won a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick at the 2003 US Open.

World No. 1 Jannik Sinner and No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz have dominated Grand Slams over the past few years, but this year's US Open provides a unique opportunity. Sinner isn't competing after a knee injury forced him to withdraw 10 days before the tournament started, and Alcaraz is just coming back from a four-month absence after dealing with his own injury.

In other words, it's anyone's tournament to win. Of course, Alcaraz is the favorite, assuming he's at peak form, and Zverev has to be a clear No. 2. He sits above 7,000 live ranking points, while no other player in the field has more than 3,900. But Shelton and Fritz remain outside contenders to end the American drought on home hardcourt.

Shelton's recent Montreal Masters 1000 title snapped a streak of early exits in big tournaments, including the French Open and Wimbledon. He likes playing in big matches, is healthier than he was earlier in the year and will have the support of the American crowd. Former American tennis star and ESPN analyst Patrick McEnroe has Shelton's back, too.

"I'm picking Big Ben," McEnroe told SportsBoom . "I'm going for it. I like Shelton to win the Open. I can stop getting this question after 20-some years: When is the next American going to win a major? I'm sick of it! I'm tired of it."

McEnroe admits Alcaraz is the favorite, even with the long absence, but the Americans have their best chance in recent memory. Shelton isn't blind to the situation.

"I think to kind of discredit the group that is playing high-level tennis right now wouldn't be smart," Shelton said. "Going into a tournament like this, I think I always have respect for whoever is playing. I try not to over-respect my opponents, obviously. But I think it is a very important part of who I am as a person and how I look at my tennis game and the tournaments I'm playing in."

First things first: Shelton needs to beat Griekspoor in the first round on Monday at 7 p.m. ET. Only then can he start to worry about the rest of the bracket.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz regresa a lo grande y presenta candidatura a retener la corona
articles.standfirst: El murciano vence y convence ante el ruso Safiullin en tres sets y no nota los 139 días de inactividad
articles.summary: El murciano vence y convence ante el ruso Safiullin en tres sets y no nota los 139 días de inactividad
articles.body: La famosa canción de Bad Bunny dice: Si te-quieres divertir con encanto y con primor sólo-tienes que vivir (¿pá dónde?) Un verano en-Nueva York (¡Nueva York!). Carlos Alcaraz, que se dejó la voz en uno de los conciertos del cantante puertorriqueño en el Metropolitano, hizo divertir en el barrio neoyorquino de Queens a los miles de aficionados que poblaban este lunes la Arthur Ashe. En la ciudad de los rascacielos, en la que reinó en 2022 y 2025, Carlitos empezó de manera brillante su andadura hacia la consecución de su octavo título del Grand Slam. Desde 2008, con Roger Federer, nadie ha sido capaz de defender la corona. El murciano está ya a seis triunfos tras acabar con la resistencia de Roman Safiullin, por 6-4, 6-4 y 6-4. Este miércoles, en la segunda ronda, le espera el portugués Jaime Faria, el 72 del ranking ATP y que viene de estrenar su casillero de triunfos en el cuarto grande del calendario. Desde su debut en los 'majors' jamás le ha fallado a la segunda ronda. Ya son 21 consecutivas, acercándose al récord en la Era Open de su idolatrado Rafael Nadal, con 34. Las dudas sobre el rendimiento en pista de Alcaraz, tras sus 139 días de inactividad por la muñeca, se disiparon cuando conectó una derecha ganadora en el séptimo juego y que le daba el primer 'break'. El jugador de El Palmar lo celebró con una mirada a su banquillo. La vara de medir de su tenis está en la fluidez con su derecha. Safiullin también salió con una malla en su brazo derecho, la misma que utiliza el campeón de siete grandes desde que se borró del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati. Le da una mayor seguridad en el golpeo. El ruso dispuso de la primera pelota de rotura en el segundo juego. Falló estrepitosamente después con una bola fácil en la red. Tuvo una segunda oportunidad después que también desperdició. Samuel López daba instrucciones a su pupilo y no tenía que recurrir a los gritos ni a las señas. Y es que la dirección del torneo ha acercado los banquillos a las esquinas de los estadios principales. Roman, con poco que perder y mucho que ganar, empezó a pegarle a la pelota como si no hubiera un mañana. Se llevó en blanco el servicio de Alcaraz y situó el segundo set con un marcador favorable de 2-0. El tenista natural de Podolsk disfrutó de un punto para el 3-0. Pero la balanza de sus errores no forzados era mayor que la de los tiros ganadores. No distingue entre pegarle fuerte y meterla dentro. Otra derecha ganadora del número tres mundial le dio el tercer break. Puño en alto. Con la maquinaria engrasada, aceleró hacia la victoria. La organización cerró el techo retráctil de la central por la amenaza de lluvia. A Carlitos le dio tiempo para dar espectáculo con un recital de voleas. Ganó 19 de las 24 que intentó ante los gritos de asombro de los aficionados.

articles.title: US Open Tennis 2026 Results, Day 2 Bracket Winners, Losers, Highlights and Day 3 Schedule
articles.summary: On Monday, Carlos Alcaraz began his US Open title defense with a straight-set win over Roman Safiullin.
articles.body:
On Monday, Carlos Alcaraz began his US Open title defense with a straight-set win over Roman Safiullin.

The 23-year-old had not played a singles match since mid-April due to a wrist injury but showed no signs of rust in his return.

In the women's draw, Aryna Sabalenka kickstarted her quest for a third straight US Open title with a straight-set win over Camila Osorio.

Below, you'll find analysis of the top matches as well as tomorrow's schedule and more.

No. 2 Carlos Alcaraz def. Roman Safiullin, 6-4, 6-4, 6-4

Stefanos Tsitsipas def. No. 10 Arthur Fils, 4-6, 7-6 (3), 6-1, 6-4

No. 22 Valentin Vacherot def. Aleksandar Kovacevic, 6-2, 6-3, 7-5

No. 23 Andrey Rublev def. Otto Virtanen, 6-7 (5), 6-7 (0), 6-0, 6-2, 7-6 (5)

Rei Sakamoto def. Aleksandar Vukic, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-3, 3-6, 6-4

Jurji Rodionov def. Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard, 7-6 (2), 6-0, 7-6 (4)

Sebastian Gorzny def. Raphael Collignon, 3-6, 6-3, 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (9)

Adrian Mannarino def. Thiago Agustin Tirante, 4-6, 3-6, 6-3, 6-3, 6-3

Carlos Alcaraz looked stellar in his return to tennis, defeating Roman Safiullin in straight sets.

The defending champion entered the US Open on the heels of a four-month-long absence due to a wrist injury.

However, Alcaraz alleviated concerns rather quickly, impressing with his forehand and top-tier fitness.

Though Alcaraz did not hit his serve at top speeds, he saved 5 of 6 break points and dominated at the net, winning 19 of 24 points.

In other action, Stefanos Tsitsipas upset Arthur Fils in four sets, earning his first top 10 win at a major since 2022.

Fils had entered off the heels of winning the Cincinnati Open and was considered a strong contender to win the US Open.

However, Tsitsipas played impressive tennis, showing why he was a top-3 player in 2021.

The first round of the US Open will continue Tuesday on ESPN, with all matches also being available on ESPN Unlimited.

Below, you can find the schedule for Tuesday's play:

Nishesh Basavareddy vs. Tristan Schoolkate

Flavio Cobolli (5) vs. Francisco Comesana

Francisco Cerundolo (24) vs. Filip Misolic

Camilo Ugo Carabelli vs. Jan-Lennard Struff

Rafael Jodar (12) vs. Thanasi Kokkinakis

Jan Choinski vs. Botic Van De Zandschulp

Match of the Day: Taylor Fritz (9) vs. Darwin Blanch

Taylor Fritz enters the US Open with hopes of reaching a Grand Slam final for the second time in his career.

The 28-year-old American has played quite well on the hard-court swing this summer, winning the Citi Open while reaching the quarterfinal at the Cincinnati Open.

Fritz possesses the tools necessary for another deep run with his booming serve and heavy groundstrokes.

American compatriot Darwin Blanch can also do damage with his serve and heavy forehand; however, he has struggled to pile up consistent results as of late, making the prospects of pulling off an upset of this caliber extremely unlikely.

Prediction: No. 9 Taylor Fritz def. Darwin Blanch in 4 sets

Aryna Sabalenka opened up her title defense with a straight-set win over Camila Osorio.

Despite entering the tournament in shakier form than usual, the world No. 1 performed as expected.

Sabalenka dictated the match on her first serve while dominating with her signature aggressive-yet-consistent baseline play.

articles.standfirst: El murciano y el portugués se cruzarán por primera vez en el circuito profesional
articles.summary: El murciano y el portugués se cruzarán por primera vez en el circuito profesional
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, tras superar la primera ronda del US Open ante Roman Safiullin, tendrá una jornada de descanso antes de medirse este miércoles a Jaime Faria en la segunda ronda del torneo neoyorquino. No hay precedentes entre el murciano y el portugués, que ocupa en la actualidad el puesto 72 del ranking ATP a sus 23 años, la misma edad de Carlitos. La victoria de Faria en el debut ante Jenson Brooksby (ya se habían enfrentado en Cincinnati con el mismo resultado) le convirtió en el tenista más joven de su país capaz de sumar victorias en los cuatro Grand Slam. Los otros dos fueron Joao Sousa (2016) y Nuno Borges (2025). El segundo partido de Carlitos en el torneo se disputará este miércoles 2 de septiembre en la pista central Arthur Ashe del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, en un horario todavía por confirmar. El partido entre Carlos Alcaraz y Jaime Faria del US Open se podrá ver en Movistar+. También podrás seguir la última hora y todo lo que ocurra en el encuentro a través de MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: 2026 US Open: Carlos Alcaraz authors straight-sets victory over Roman Safiullin in first singles match back
articles.summary: The first chapter of Alcaraz's comeback was convincing.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz pumped his fist and put his hand to his ear, reveling in the moment Monday at the US Open.

He authored a 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 victory over Russian Roman Safiullin in his first singles match since April when he injured his right wrist at the Barcelona Open. It's his first major since since he won the Australian Open this past winter , a triumph made him the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam .

The Spaniard has won the US Open twice before, including last year when he defeated Italy's Jannik Sinner in the final. Sinner, the world No. 1, isn't taking part in the major this time around because of a right knee injury that he's been nursing .

Notably, Alcaraz won't have to face fourth-seeded Novak Djokovic, either. Djokovic could have stood in Alcaraz's path to the final, but the 39-year-old Serbian suffered an agonizing five-set defeat in the first round on Sunday night to Argentine Mariano Navone .

Alcaraz made his return to competition last week during the mixed doubles portion of the US Open. He followed up his absence by teaming up with a 44-year-old Serena Williams.

Together, the tennis superstars — one on a path to the sport's Mount Rushmore and the other already there — bested doubles specialists Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool before bowing out in the the quarterfinals to the fourth-seeded team of Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli . That more casual event served as Alcaraz's brief ramp-up to the US Open singles draw. Earlier this month, he withdrew from the Cincinnati Open , which is regarded as the warmup tournament for the US Open.

At the time, the 23-year-old Alcaraz was still navigating his wrist issue and working his way back to tournament-level play. He was dealing with tenosynovitis, which, according to Cleveland Clinic , is the inflammation of the connective tissue that surrounds your tendons. It can be painful and inhibit joint movement.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion has a chance to pull off a stunning comeback in Queens, given his limited play in the past four-plus months leading up to the singles draw.

That reboot is off to a swift start, with Alcaraz taking care of business in straight sets on Monday at Arthur Ashe Stadium.
